title: The Emporium by Thorton Wilder completed by Kirk Lynn at Classic Stag...
transcript: For much of Act 1, The Emporium is just as frustratingly elusive as the titular department store that it's about. An unfinished play by Thornton Wilder now Frankensteined together by Kirk Lynn, it follows a young man named John on a quest to move to the big city and work at The Emporium — exactly how or why is unclear. It's a slow and confusing start, but if you lean into the opacity, it becomes a lot more enjoyable. While the details are pretty fuzzy, the nature of labor emerges as a thematic anchor, as does the distinction between making a living and making a life. I noticed some similarities to Thornton Wilder's other two plays that helped frame my interpretations going into intermission, after which point things only went downhill. The audience votes on whether or not they wish to see a prologue at the top of Act 2 where the actors explicitly state what the play represents and they demystify the allegory. I'd argue that giving us an opportunity to have this explanation is really at odds with the fact that the play was unfinished, and it makes me wonder if the choice is there just to placate an impatient audience. At my performance, it was 31-8 for the prologue, and it totally soured Act 2 for me, partially because the metaphor was pretty aligned with how I had already been interpreting it. Although viewing Act 2 through a definitive lens made it more emotionally resonant and shed more light on the directorial choices, it also stripped of any intrigue or nuance. Once it was all spelled out, I simply wasn't invested anymore, and I realized that the puzzle of the play was far more interesting than the story itself. With that, another program for my collection.
reasoning: The reviewer describes a slow, confusing Act 1 that became enjoyable if you leaned in, but Act 2 'went downhill' and he 'wasn't invested anymore.' The overall verdict leans negative, concluding the puzzle was more interesting than the story.
